name: read_material
description:
Inspect a Material, Material Instance, or Material Function. Materials are data-flow graphs (no execution pins): expression nodes feed their outputs into other nodes' inputs and ultimately into the material's root property inputs (BaseColor, Metallic, Roughness, Normal, EmissiveColor, Opacity, etc.).

Modes:
- describe (default): full node graph — every expression node (id, class, title, position, parameter name), each node's inputs and which upstream node/output feeds them, plus the root property connections. Works on base Materials and Material Functions (not Instances). A MaterialFunctionCall node is opaque in the parent graph but carries a "function" field with the called function's asset path — call read_material on that path to descend into MF_* internals. Function describes also list function_inputs/function_outputs (the call node's pins).
- overview: settings + parameter inventory — material domain, blend mode, shading model, two-sided, Substrate flag, and the scalar/vector/texture/static-switch parameters WITH their current values. Each parameter is {name, value} on base Materials; on Material Instances each is {name, value, overridden, parent_value} so you can see exactly which overrides are set and what they inherit. Vector values are [r,g,b,a]; texture values are asset paths. Works for base Materials, Material Instances (which also report their parent and have no graph), and Material Functions (interface + expression count only). Use this to verify set_material_instance_parameter results.

Node ids are the expression object names (e.g. "MaterialExpressionMultiply_0"); reference them when editing.

material.description: Asset path of the Material, Material Instance, or Material Function (e.g. "/Game/Materials/M_Rock" or "/Game/Materials/Functions/MF_Outline").

mode.description: describe = node graph (base Materials and Material Functions); overview = settings + parameters (Materials, Instances, Functions). Defaults to describe.

name: create_material_expression
description:
Add one expression node to a base Material's graph and return its id + real pins. Drives UMaterialEditingLibrary::CreateMaterialExpression.

The 'node' is a friendly expression type name — the leading "MaterialExpression" prefix is optional and matching is case-insensitive (e.g. "Multiply", "Add", "LinearInterpolate"/"Lerp", "TextureSample", "ScalarParameter", "VectorParameter", "Constant3Vector", "Fresnel", "Panner", "TextureCoordinate", "ComponentMask", "AppendVector"). For parameter expressions, pass parameter_name to name the parameter.

Returns the new node's id (use it in edit_material), inputs, and outputs. Creating a node does not connect it — follow with edit_material to set property values and wire it, then compile_material to verify. Prefer adding parameters (Scalar/Vector/Texture) so variants can be made as Material Instances rather than new base materials.

material.description: Asset path of the base Material.

pos_x.description: Graph X position (optional; negative is left/upstream).

parameter_name.description: For parameter expressions: the parameter's name (optional).

name: edit_material
description:
Batch-edit a base Material's graph, then recompile to verify. Reference nodes by the ids returned from read_material/create_material_expression.

Operations (array, applied in order):
- {"action":"set_property","node":"<id>","property":"<UProperty>","value":<v>} — set a node property. Examples: Constant.R (number), Constant3Vector.Constant ([r,g,b] or [r,g,b,a]), ScalarParameter.DefaultValue (number), VectorParameter.DefaultValue ([r,g,b,a]), Parameter.ParameterName (string), TextureSample.Texture (asset path), StaticSwitchParameter.DefaultValue (bool).
- {"action":"connect","from_node":"<id>","from_output":"","to_node":"<id>","to_input":"A"} — wire one expression output into another's input. from_output "" = first output; to_input is the pin name (e.g. "A", "B", "UVs", "Alpha").
- {"action":"connect","from_node":"<id>","from_output":"","to_property":"BaseColor"} — wire an output into a material root property (BaseColor, Metallic, Roughness, Normal, EmissiveColor, Opacity, OpacityMask, AmbientOcclusion, WorldPositionOffset, ...).
- {"action":"disconnect","to_node":"<id>","to_input":"A"} or {"action":"disconnect","to_property":"BaseColor"} — clear an input.
- {"action":"delete_node","node":"<id>"}.

For domain="UI", the editor label "Final Color" maps to the API root property "EmissiveColor". Use to_property:"EmissiveColor" for UI color; display labels are not API property identifiers.

Mind value types: float vs float3. A connection that fails returns success:false with a reason — fix pin names/types. Set atomic:true to revert all operations if any fail; the revert is verified (status "rolled_back", outcome.recovery_status "restored"). status "rollback_incomplete" (retry_safe=false) means part of the batch may remain: re-read the material, do not resend. Recompiles automatically and returns compile errors.

material.description: Asset path of the base Material.

atomic.description: Revert all operations if any fails, verified against the pre-batch material (default false). Check recovery_status: only "restored" means unchanged.

to_property.description: Root property API name. UI Final Color is EmissiveColor.

name: create_material_instance
description:
Create a Material Instance Constant (MIC) — the PREFERRED way to make a material variant. Instead of authoring a new base material or duplicating one, create an instance of an existing parameterized material and override its parameters. Instances reuse the parent's compiled shader (nearly free), so studios keep a few master materials + many instances.

Reach for this first whenever the request is "make a red version", "a rougher variant", "swap the texture", etc. Only edit a base material's graph when no parameter exposes the needed change.

After creating, use set_material_instance_parameter to override values (read_material mode='overview' on the parent lists the available parameter names).

name.description: Name for the new instance, e.g. "MI_Rock_Red".

parent.description: Asset path of the parent Material or Material Instance to inherit from.

name: set_material_instance_parameter
description:
Override parameters on a Material Instance Constant, then refresh it. This is how you customize a variant created with create_material_instance.

Each parameter has a type (scalar|vector|texture|switch), a name (must match a parameter exposed by the parent material — see read_material overview), and a value:
- scalar: a number (e.g. 0.3)
- vector: [r,g,b] or [r,g,b,a]
- texture: an asset path string
- switch: a boolean (static switch)

'parameters' is ONE FLAT array of {type, name, value} objects — no wrapper objects, no nesting. Example:
{"instance": "/Game/Materials/MI_Rock_Red", "parameters": [
  {"type": "scalar", "name": "Roughness", "value": 0.3},
  {"type": "vector", "name": "Tint", "value": [1, 0, 0, 1]}
]}

Only the named parameters are overridden; everything else inherits from the parent. Verify with read_material mode='overview' on the instance, which reports each parameter's current value and override state.

instance.description: Asset path of the Material Instance Constant.

name.description: Parameter name as exposed by the parent material.

name: manage_material
description:
Change a base Material's shading settings, then recompile. Only the fields you provide are changed. Use read_material mode='overview' first to see current settings.

Settings:
- blend_mode: Opaque, Masked, Translucent, Additive, Modulate, AlphaComposite, AlphaHoldout
- shading_model: DefaultLit, Unlit, Subsurface, PreintegratedSkin, ClearCoat, SubsurfaceProfile, TwoSidedFoliage, Hair, Cloth, Eye, SingleLayerWater, ThinTranslucent
- domain: Surface, DeferredDecal, LightFunction, Volume, PostProcess, UI. Use "UI" for the editor's "User Interface" domain
- two_sided: boolean

Affects the whole material (and every instance of it). Bare names ('Opaque') or prefixed names ('BLEND_Opaque') are both accepted.

material.description: Asset path of the base Material.

domain.description: API domain name. UI is the editor User Interface domain.

name: compile_material
description:
Recompile a base Material's shaders and report errors plus instruction/sampler statistics. This is the verify step after authoring or editing a material's graph — always call it once edits are done.

Returns: success/status, any shader compile errors, and statistics (vertex/pixel instruction counts, sampler count, texture samples). Watch the sampler count — the hard limit is 16. Note: instruction/sampler stats require compiled shaders and may read 0 in a headless run (check statistics.available).

Only applies to base Materials; Material Instances inherit their parent's shaders and cannot be compiled directly.

material.description: Asset path of the base Material to recompile (e.g. "/Game/Materials/M_Rock").
